It runs northeast to southwest for about 35 kilometres and forms part of the boundary between the Nelson and Tasman Districts and the Marlborough Region. Several peaks exceed 1,000 metres, notably Saddle Hill at 1,215 metres and Mount Duppa at 1,133 metres. This photograph was taken on 25 April 2019 at 10:03 on the trail between Rocks Hut and Middle Creek Hut, a section of the Te Araroa Trail, as the sun broke through morning fog in the bush.
feed.lookAt: Fog is what makes the light visible: the sunbeams only show because mist hangs in the trees. Point toward the sun, keep the brightest rays off a dark trunk so they read, and let the fallen log in the foreground anchor the lower left of the frame.

feed.title: Cotton hoers near Clarksdale, Mississippi

image.credit: Dorothea Lange, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Dorothea Lange made this photograph in June or July 1937 near Clarksdale, Mississippi, and captioned it: These cotton hoers work from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. for $1.00. Born Dorothea Margaretta Nutzhorn in 1895, she became a documentary photographer best known for her Depression-era work for the Farm Security Administration, and her images humanized the consequences of the Great Depression. Her Migrant Mother of 1936 became the defining image of the Dust Bowl. Here a line of African American workers walks away from the camera along a field path, hoes over their shoulders, under a bright summer sky.
feed.lookAt: Lange stood behind the workers and let them walk away, which turns individuals into a line and gives the scene its weight. The hoes make a rhythm of diagonals. Shooting from behind keeps faces private while telling the story through posture, tools and clothing.

feed.title: Mueller Hut and Mount Sefton at sunrise

image.credit: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Mount Sefton, Maukatua in Māori, is a mountain in the Aroarokaehe Range of the Southern Alps, just 12 kilometres south of Aoraki / Mount Cook. At 3,151 metres it is the thirteenth-highest peak in the Southern Alps. Tuckett Glacier flows down its south-eastern side and Mueller Glacier lies in the valley below. Julius von Haast named it for William Sefton Moorhouse, and Edward FitzGerald, guided by Matthias Zurbriggen, made the first recorded climb shortly after Christmas 1894. Michal Klajban made this panorama at 5:45 on 16 January 2020, at sunrise, with Mueller Hut in the frame.
feed.lookAt: At first light the highest rock catches the sun while the snowfield below stays cool and blue. That temperature split is the picture. The small red hut at the right edge gives the peaks a scale, and the pale sky leaves room for the long summit ridge.

caption.title: Mueller Hut and Mount Sefton at sunrise
caption.line2: Michal Klajban · Aoraki / Mount Cook National Park

feed.title: Grand Canyon from Hopi Point

image.credit: Tuxyso, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: This view of the Grand Canyon's South Rim was made from Hopi Point in warm evening light on 8 September 2013. Across the canyon stands Shiva Temple, a 2,331-metre summit about six miles north of Hopi Point that towers 1,600 metres above the Colorado River. Clarence Dutton, who began the tradition of naming Grand Canyon features after mythological deities, named it for the Hindu deity Shiva, and the name was adopted in 1906. In 1937 the American Museum of Natural History explored its isolated top hoping to find new species; the scientists found Ancestral Puebloan dwellings and an empty Kodak film box.
feed.lookAt: Evening light does the modelling here: each butte has a bright face and a dark one, so the layers read as separate steps. Low cloud sits like a band between the foreground ridges and the distant temples. Shoot long and let haze stack the depth.

feed.title: Automatic dumper at an orange packing plant, Redlands

image.credit: Jack Delano, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Jack Delano made this colour transparency in March 1943 at a co-operative orange packing plant in Redlands, California, as part of what the Library of Congress titles his Santa Fe trip. Born in the Russian Empire in 1914, he worked for the Farm Security Administration, and later settled in Puerto Rico. The picture shows an automatic dumper at work: a crate of oranges tips over a rail while oranges tumble across a wooden chute, some blurred by their motion, and another full crate waits at the top right. Dark green wood and a metal pipe cut across the frame.
feed.lookAt: The shutter was fast enough to freeze most of the oranges but slow enough to blur the ones still falling, and that blur tells you it is moving. The orange against dark green is a strong colour pair. Look for a repeat, then catch the single odd moment.

caption.title: Automatic dumper at an orange packing plant, Redlands

feed.title: Dunes in the Thar Desert

image.credit: Clément Bardot, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is an arid region in the north-west of the Indian subcontinent and one of the largest subtropical deserts in Asia, covering 264,091 square kilometres. About two-thirds lies in India, mainly in Rajasthan, with the rest in Pakistan. Its sand was built up by wind-blown sediment from the alluvial plains and the coast, after the Ghaggar-Hakra river system dried up and the Aravalli uplift changed the region's drainage. Clément Bardot photographed this dune at 14:07 on 15 February 2016, under a clear blue sky.
feed.lookAt: Sand ripples turn a plain slope into pattern: the wavy lines run toward the crest and lead the eye to the one smooth curve of the dune against the sky. Keep the horizon low and the frame simple, and let the blue sky act as a clean backdrop.

feed.title: Hidden Lake Lookout at sunset

image.credit: Nick Archibald, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Hidden Lake Lookout is a small fire lookout built in 1932 on a subsidiary peak of the Hidden Lake Peaks, in the North Cascades of Washington state, just outside North Cascades National Park. The peaks reach a maximum of 2,160 metres, ten miles east of Marblemount. The Forest Service used the lookout until it was decommissioned around 1953, and it has now stood longer as a historic monument than it served as a fire lookout; it joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1987. Nick Archibald photographed it at 20:05 on 12 August 2018, as the sun set through smoky haze from nearby fires.
feed.lookAt: Smoke from distant fires turns the sky amber and flattens the far ridges into layers. The little hut gives the scene a human scale against that haze, and the low sun at the right edge adds a point of light. Arrive early and wait for the last ten minutes.

feed.title: Porters Pass

image.credit: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Porters Pass, at 939 metres, is a mountain pass in the Canterbury region of New Zealand's South Island, near Lake Lyndon in Korowai/Torlesse Tussocklands Park. State Highway 73 crosses it on the way from Springfield to Cass, and it is the last pass on the road east from Westland to Christchurch. It is a few metres higher than the better-known Arthur's Pass. The Porter brothers, who farmed nearby, named it in 1858. Michal Klajban took this panorama on 18 July 2019 from the ridges of Foggy Peak, with snowy Ben More, the highest named summit of the Big Ben Range, behind.
feed.lookAt: From a ridge above, the highway becomes a drawn line that winds through the tussock slopes and tells you the pass's shape. The pale scree scar mid-frame acts as a bright anchor. A panorama crop keeps the road and the distant snow in one band.

feed.title: Summit view of Lascar volcano

image.credit: Alexandre Buisse (Nattfodd), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Lascar is a stratovolcano in Chile, in the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes, and the most active volcano in the region, with eruption records going back to 1848. It consists of two cones with several summit craters, and the westernmost crater of the eastern cone is presently active, releasing gas and occasional explosions. The volcano has been active for at least 56,000 years, fed by the subduction of the Nazca Plate beneath the South America Plate. Alexandre Buisse made this 360° view from almost the summit, at an altitude of 5,500 metres, on 28 September 2007; it is a downscaled stitch of eleven photographs, with smoke visible from the crater.
feed.lookAt: A 360° stitch flattens into a thin strip, but the single hiker gives it scale: a tiny dark figure against rubble slopes and a steaming crater. Include a person when you shoot in a place with no other size cues, and keep them small.

feed.title: Waterfall at the New York Botanical Garden

image.credit: King of Hearts, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The New York Botanical Garden is a botanical garden at Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City, established in 1891 on a 250-acre site that holds over one million living plants. The first structures opened at the end of that decade, and the garden has been a National Historic Landmark since 1967. It also includes the Enid A. Haupt Conservatory and a major plant research and conservation programme. This photograph shows a waterfall on the Bronx River within the grounds, made on 23 October 2016 at 15:48, in autumn, when the leaves along the bank turn yellow and orange.
feed.lookAt: A slow shutter smooths the falling water into silk while rocks and leaves stay sharp. The weir's diagonal leads from the lower left into the dark pool, where autumn colour reflects. Use a tripod or a rock and a small aperture on a gray afternoon.

caption.title: Waterfall at the New York Botanical Garden

feed.title: National Gallery Singapore atrium

image.credit: Basile Morin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The National Gallery Singapore is a public art museum in the Civic District of Singapore, housing Singaporean and Southeast Asian art from the nineteenth century to the present, with more than 9,000 artworks. It occupies two national monuments, the former Supreme Court and former City Hall, with a combined floor area of 64,000 square metres, making it the largest visual arts venue in the country. The development cost approximately S$532 million. Basile Morin made this photograph at 18:14 on 8 June 2018, in the evening, showing the airy corridors on four levels, the staircases and the escalators; the architect was Jean-François Milou.
feed.lookAt: Four floors of identical balustrades repeat like a stack, and the central void draws the eye down to the escalators. Photograph from the centre line so the symmetry holds, and wait for evening, when warm interior lights balance the cool glass roof.

feed.title: Chuquicamata open-pit mine

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Chuquicamata is a state-owned copper mine at 2,850 metres above sea level just outside Calama, in northern Chile. By excavated volume it is the largest open-pit copper mine in the world. The pit was started in 1882 as a mine for gold and copper; it is 4.5 kilometres long, 3.5 kilometres wide and 850 metres deep, making it the second deepest open-pit mine after Bingham Canyon in Utah. In 2003 the nearby town of Chuquicamata was dismantled because of environmental concerns and the mine's expansion. Diego Delso made this panorama at 19:37 on 1 February 2016 in the Atacama Desert.
feed.lookAt: Scale is the hard part, and the photographer's tip is to spot the haul truck, 9.5 metres long, on the benches far below. Terraces make a repeating pattern that draws the eye to the pit floor. Stand on the rim, keep the horizon level, and include a sliver of sky.

feed.title: Gröna Lund at dusk

image.credit: Arild Vågen, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Gröna Lund, whose name means Green Grove, is an amusement park on the seaward side of Djurgården in Stockholm, Sweden. It was founded in 1883 by Jacob Schultheis and is the first and oldest amusement park in the country. At 3.8 hectares it is relatively small, mainly because its central location limits expansion, but it has over thirty attractions and hosts concerts in summer with its three event venues. Arild Vågen made this photograph at 22:55 on 3 June 2015, at dusk, looking across the water at the roller coaster on the left, the tall towers, and the lit swing ride on the right.
feed.lookAt: Blue hour is the sweet spot: the sky is deep blue while the rides' lights are already bright enough to glow. The still water repeats every light as a streak, doubling the colour. Use a tripod and expose for the lights, not the sky.

feed.title: Visitor Center deck, Brooklyn Botanic Garden

image.credit: King of Hearts, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Brooklyn Botanic Garden is a botanical garden in the borough of Brooklyn, New York City, occupying 52 acres in central Brooklyn, close to Prospect Park and the Brooklyn Museum. The site was first designated in 1897, and the garden opened in May 1911 on the site of an ash dump, with its landscape designed by the Olmsted Brothers. It holds over 14,000 taxa of plants and has over 800,000 visitors each year. King of Hearts photographed the deck above the Visitor Center on 2 May 2015, from an angle that lines up a glass wall and slatted roof against spring greenery and a distant building.
feed.lookAt: A wide lens close to the glass roof makes its slats rush toward the vanishing point, while green foliage fills the right third. Reflections in the wall double the trees. Stand low and tilt slightly down to keep the edges converging cleanly toward the horizon.

caption.title: Visitor Center deck, Brooklyn Botanic Garden

feed.title: Milky Way over Paranal Observatory

image.credit: ESO/H.H. Heyer, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Paranal Observatory sits on Cerro Paranal in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, at 2,635 metres. The European Southern Observatory established it on 1 April 1999, and it is the largest optical-infrared observatory in the Southern Hemisphere by light-collecting area. Its Very Large Telescope has four 8.2-metre main telescopes plus four 1.8-metre auxiliary ones. This 360-degree panorama by ESO's H.H. Heyer, dated 9 November 2009, shows the Moon just rising with zodiacal light above it, the Milky Way arching across the sky, and the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds low on the right, with the open telescope domes along the left.
feed.lookAt: A 360-degree stitch turns the whole sky into one band, so the Milky Way becomes a giant arch that frames the dark horizon. The small domes at the left give the sky its scale. Shoot night panoramas from a tripod, rotate level, and keep a low, flat foreground.

feed.title: Cloudscape over La Silla Observatory

image.credit: ESO/F. Kamphues, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: La Silla Observatory stands on the southern edge of the Atacama Desert in the north of Chile's Coquimbo region, 150 kilometres northeast of La Serena. It was the first site in Chile used by the European Southern Observatory, which runs three major telescopes there: the 3.6-metre telescope, the New Technology Telescope and the 2.2-metre Max-Planck-ESO telescope. Like Paranal, it has some of the darkest night skies on Earth. F. Kamphues made this 360-degree view of a rare cloudscape in early December 2009. The dome at the centre belongs to the 3.6-metre telescope, and the sun sets under red clouds at the left.
feed.lookAt: Clouds are rare here, so the photographer let them become the subject: the low sun paints a red band along the horizon and the sky stays moody and layered. Look for conditions that are unusual at a place, and expose for the glowing clouds so the domes stay dark shapes.

feed.title: Twenty-mule-team borax wagons, Harmony Borax Works

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith photographed these borax wagons at the Harmony Borax Works in Death Valley on 20 December 2012. The image belongs to the Jon B. Lovelace Collection of California Photographs in her America Project, which she has donated to the Library of Congress since 1992; she says her work documents the landscapes, architecture and people of the United States. The Harmony works began producing borax in late 1883, and each wagon train was pulled by 20 animals, usually 18 mules and two horses. Here a riveted, rust-red water tank and a wooden box wagon stand on gravel, with their big spoked wheels filling the lower frame.
feed.lookAt: She put the lens close to the front wheel, so its spokes sweep across the foreground and the long wagon train recedes behind. The rusty red against a clean blue sky is a simple colour pair. Move close to a big object and let its parts lead into the distance.

caption.title: Twenty-mule-team borax wagons, Harmony Borax Works
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, interior

image.credit: Basile Morin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Marina Bay Sands is an integrated resort fronting Marina Bay in Singapore and a landmark of the city. At its opening in 2010 it was deemed the world's most expensive standalone casino property at S$8 billion. The resort includes a 1,850-room hotel, a convention centre, a theatre, an ArtScience museum and a 74,000-square-metre luxury mall, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands. Basile Morin photographed the mall's interior on 5 June 2018, in the late afternoon, looking along illuminated corridors, an escalator and the transparent glass vaulted roof that curves overhead and drops away down the length of the building.
feed.lookAt: Stand at a railing above the corridor and the glass ribs sweep across the frame, drawing your eye to the far end. A wide lens and a level horizon keep the curves clean. A slow shutter lets passers-by blur at the left while the architecture stays sharp.

caption.title: Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, interior

feed.title: Taj Palace Hotel and Gateway of India, Mumbai

image.credit: iMahesh, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Gateway of India stands on the waterfront of Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea. It was built to commemorate the landing in India of King George V and Queen Mary on 2 December 1911, the first visit of a British monarch to India. The Scottish architect George Wittet designed it in yellow basalt and reinforced concrete, with perforated screens from Gwalior; it is 26 metres high and was opened on 4 December 1924. In this panorama from 7 November 2023, iMahesh looks across the harbour from the water, with the Taj Palace Hotel and Taj Tower rising beside the arch, and ferries lined up in front.
feed.lookAt: The photographer stepped back far enough to include the harbour boats, so a famous monument reads as part of a working waterfront. The red dome, the tower and the arch each balance the frame. When you shoot a landmark, include the context that explains the place.

caption.title: Taj Palace Hotel and Gateway of India, Mumbai

feed.title: Pond and fountain at the Houston Zoo

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith titled this picture A boy enjoys a lovely pond and fountain away from the animals at the Houston, Texas, zoo, and made it on 2 May 2014. It belongs to the Lyda Hill Texas Collection of Photographs in her America Project, a gift to the Library of Congress. The Houston Zoo is in Hermann Park, opened in 1922 and covers 55 acres. In her frame, large oaks spread a canopy over a long rectangular pond with two fountains and a bronze figure on a pedestal. A boy runs along the path at the left, and sunlight breaks into patches on the paving.
feed.lookAt: Dappled light on the path leads the eye past the boy toward the pond, and the oak canopy frames the scene from above. Exposure is set for the shade, so the bright patches nearly burn out. Use a small figure and a strong light pattern to make a quiet place feel alive.

caption.title: Pond and fountain at the Houston Zoo
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: Trebišnjica valley at Gornji Orahovac

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Gornji Orahovac, also written Gornji Orovac, is a village in the municipality of Trebinje, in Republika Srpska, Bosnia and Herzegovina. It covers about 3.5 square kilometres and lies at roughly 640 metres. The Trebišnjica river runs through the valley below it. Diego Delso made this panoramic view on 14 April 2014, shortly after ten in the morning, from a hillside above the valley. The river bends in a bright turquoise ribbon between green slopes and a pale limestone mountainside on the right, while small fields and a few houses scatter the valley floor and hazy ridges fade into the distance.
feed.lookAt: A high vantage and a long panoramic crop let the river's S-curve lead the eye across the valley. The turquoise water is the one saturated colour in a green and grey scene. Climb above a river bend and wait for its colour to stand out.

feed.title: Gopuram of Sri Mariamman Temple, Singapore

image.credit: AngMoKio, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Sri Mariamman Temple is a Hindu temple at 244 South Bridge Road, Singapore. It was founded in 1827 by Naraina Pillai and was gazetted a national monument on 6 July 1973. The entrance tower, called a gopuram, was first built in 1903 with three tiers; the present six-tiered tower dates from 1925. AngMoKio photographed a detail of the gopuram on 15 February 2011, climbing the frame up through the tiers. Rows of painted figures sit on every ledge, dressed in blue, red, green and yellow, with raised hands, moustaches and ornate crowns, and curling scrollwork between the tiers.
feed.lookAt: Shot from below with a tight crop, the tower becomes a vertical pattern of faces and gestures. Repetition gives the frame its rhythm, and each small colour block is balanced by its neighbours. Fill the frame with texture, then look for the one figure that breaks the pattern.

caption.title: Gopuram of Sri Mariamman Temple, Singapore

feed.title: The 19-story cross near Groom, Texas

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith made this photograph on 1 June 2014, at about 7:43 in the evening. Her title describes a 19-story-high cross, erected by the nonprofit Cross Ministries along U.S. 40 (the old U.S. Route 66) near Groom in the Texas Panhandle. The Lyda Hill Texas Collection of Photographs in her America Project holds it at the Library of Congress. Wikipedia describes the cross as 190 feet tall with fourteen life-sized statues of the Stations of the Cross around its base. Here the white cross stands against a dark storm cloud, lit by low evening sun, with small statues, trees and open grass at its foot.
feed.lookAt: A vertical frame, a dark thundercloud and low sidelight make the white cross glow. The few statues and trees at the base give it a scale you can feel. When the sky turns dramatic, step back, align the vertical straight, and let the light pick out the subject.

caption.title: The 19-story cross near Groom, Texas
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: Mandrem Beach and creek, Goa

image.credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Mandrem is a coastal village in Pernem taluka, in North Goa district of Goa, India, 21 kilometres from the state capital Panaji. It had a population of 8,336 at the 2011 census. Mandrem Beach lies between the twin beaches of Morjim and Arambol, and a tidal creek, also called the Mandrem River, runs parallel to the shore and meets the sea at high tide. The beach is a notified turtle nesting site for Olive Ridley turtles. Vyacheslav Argenberg photographed it in January 2011, when thatched shelters and loungers stood on both banks of the creek and a bamboo footbridge crossed it.
feed.lookAt: The creek curves from the lower right toward the surf line and pulls your eye out to sea. Thatched shelters on both banks give the frame depth and scale. A slightly raised position separates sand, water and horizon into clean bands.

feed.title: Ngaben procession at the sea, Nusa Penida

image.credit: Imadedana, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Nusa Penida is an island off southeast Bali, in Indonesia, separated from Bali by the Badung Strait. Its interior is hilly, with a maximum altitude of 524 metres, and its climate is drier than Bali's. It is a major tourist destination; the district had an estimated 65,820 people in 2024. Imadedana photographed a ngaben on 6 August 2021. Ngaben is a Balinese ritual for the dead, and in this aerial view bearers wade through shallow turquoise water carrying a bamboo platform topped with an ornate tower and a black bull figure, with outrigger boats waiting beyond.
feed.lookAt: The photographer shot from above, which turns the bearers into a dense pattern around the platform and shows how far the group is moving into the water. The bright tower and dark bull stand out against turquoise. Try an overhead angle when a crowd moves together.

caption.title: Ngaben procession at the sea, Nusa Penida

feed.title: Women working in a needlework factory, Santurce

image.credit: Jack Delano, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Jack Delano made this photograph in January 1942 in the Rodriguez needlework factory in Santurce, Puerto Rico, where, the Library of Congress notes, the minimum wage was six dollars a week. Delano was born in the Russian Empire in 1914, worked for the Farm Security Administration, and later spent much of his life in Puerto Rico. His wide view looks down a long room of sewing machines, with women bent over their work at each station. White spools of thread and drifts of cloth fill the foreground, and rows of columns and windows recede into the building, so the viewer sees the scale of the workroom.
feed.lookAt: Tilting the camera down the room puts rows of machines on a diagonal that runs from the foreground to the far wall. White thread spools repeat across the frame and give the dark workers and floor a rhythm. Show an entire workplace, and the labour and the space explain each other.

caption.title: Women working in a needlework factory, Santurce

feed.title: Grand Hotel, Saltsjöbaden, in winter

image.credit: Arild Vågen, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Saltsjöbaden is a locality in Nacka Municipality, Stockholm County, Sweden, on the Baltic Sea coast deep in the Stockholm Archipelago. Its Grand Hotel was built on the initiative of Knut Agathon Wallenberg and opened by King Oscar II in 1893. The Saltsjöbaden Agreement was signed there on 20 December 1938, and the hotel hosted Bilderberg meetings in 1962, 1973 and 1984. Arild Vågen photographed it from the air on 2 February 2013. Snow lies on the roofs and grounds, ice covers the bay, and a long pier runs out across the frozen water toward the camera.
feed.lookAt: From the air in winter, the pale hotel sits between snow and ice with only dark roofs for contrast. The pier cuts a straight line through the soft shapes of the frozen bay. Wait for snow to simplify a scene, then use one hard line as an anchor.

feed.title: Baobab in Makgadikgadi Pans National Park

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Makgadikgadi Pan is a salt pan in the middle of the dry savanna of north-eastern Botswana, one of the largest salt flats in the world. It is all that remains of the enormous Lake Makgadikgadi, which once covered an area larger than Switzerland and dried up tens of thousands of years ago. Studies of human mitochondrial DNA suggest modern Homo sapiens began to evolve here some 200,000 years ago. Diego Delso photographed a baobab, Adansonia digitata, in a typical landscape of Makgadikgadi Pans National Park on 30 July 2018, soon after sunrise, with the tree standing leafless on the left.
feed.lookAt: A leafless baobab on the left third balances a long empty plain, and a dirt track bends into the grass. The deep blue sky gives the golden light a clean backdrop. Place a lone subject off-centre and let space around it speak for the landscape.

caption.title: Baobab in Makgadikgadi Pans National Park

feed.title: Ge'nyen Massif from Litang

image.credit: Zhangzhugang, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Ge'nyen Massif is a mountain in the Shaluli Mountains of western Sichuan province, China. At 6,204 metres it is the third highest peak in the province and was first climbed in 1988 by a Japanese team. It is regarded as the 13th most holy mountain among the 24 holy mountains of Tibetan Buddhism, and Lenggu Monastery sits in a steep valley at the foot of its eastern flank. Zhangzhugang made this wide panorama on 16 September 2014 and labelled it as Litang, in the file description. Green grassland rolls up to a long ridge, and clouds hang above the dark slopes.
feed.lookAt: A very wide, short crop keeps the grassland, ridge and cloud as three horizontal layers, so the mountain feels huge without a single peak in the frame. Think about panoramic crops when the land is long and the light is soft.

feed.title: Climber on the summit ridge of Island Peak

image.credit: Mountaineer, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Island Peak, also called Imja Tse, is a mountain in Sagarmatha National Park in the Himalayas of eastern Nepal. Members of the British Mount Everest expedition named it Island Peak in 1953 because it appears as an island in a sea of ice when seen from Dingboche; it was renamed Imja Tse in 1983. The southwest summit was first climbed in 1953 as part of a training exercise for that expedition. This photograph, taken on 27 October 2004, shows a climber taking the final steps toward the 6,189-metre summit along a narrow snow ridge, clipped to a rope, with clouds filling the valley below.
feed.lookAt: The rope and the ridge create two strong diagonals that lead to the climber, and the red pack stands out against the white. Dark peaks and cloud in the background show how high the ridge is. Shoot a figure small enough to show scale, but bright enough to read.

caption.title: Climber on the summit ridge of Island Peak

feed.title: New house frame, Kampung Salarom, Sabah

image.credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Sabah is a state of Malaysia in northern Borneo, in the region of East Malaysia. Kota Kinabalu is the state capital and economic centre, and the 2020 census recorded a population of 3,418,785. Sabah has an equatorial climate, and shares maritime borders with Vietnam and the Philippines. Uwe Aranas photographed this scene on 20 May 2014 in Kampung Salarom, Sapulut, Sabah. According to the file description, a carpenter was working on the frame of a newly built, traditional house. The bare timber frame stands on tall posts with a ladder against it and crossing roof beams, under a bright sky.
feed.lookAt: A house without walls shows how it is made, and the beams and posts become a drawing of lines against the sky. Shoot from a low angle so the timbers cross against the clouds. A construction site is a good place to look for structure.

caption.title: New house frame, Kampung Salarom, Sabah

feed.title: Esplanade Bridge and the Central Business District at dusk

image.credit: Basile Morin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Esplanade Bridge is a 261-metre road bridge across the mouth of the Singapore River, with the Esplanade theatres on its northern abutment and the Merlion on the southern. The low concrete arched bridge, 70 metres wide, has seven spans and carries two four-lane carriageways with walkways on both sides. Construction began in early 1994 and finished in March 1997. Basile Morin photographed it on 6 June 2018, in the evening, looking toward the skyline of the Central Business District and The Fullerton Hotel. Tower lights glow warm against a blue sky, and their reflections run in long gold streaks across the calm water.
feed.lookAt: Blue hour balances the sky and the lit windows, so neither is lost. The low bridge cuts a calm horizontal through the towers, and the water doubles the lights in warm streaks. Use a tripod and shoot just after sunset, when sky and city have similar brightness.

caption.title: Esplanade Bridge and the Central Business District at dusk

feed.title: Sweeping volcanic ash, Yogyakarta

image.credit: Crisco 1492, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Kelud is a stratovolcano in Kediri, East Java, Indonesia. Like many Indonesian volcanoes on the Pacific Ring of Fire, it is known for large explosive eruptions, and more than 30 have occurred since 1000 AD. It last erupted on 13 February 2014, destroying the lava dome and throwing boulders, stones and ash as far as West Java, about 500 kilometres away. Crisco 1492 photographed this scene in Yogyakarta on 14 February 2014, the day after. A man in a conical hat and face mask bends over a broom on a street thick with grey ash, while dusty vehicles and a sack stand along the kerb.
feed.lookAt: The red jacket is the only strong colour in a street gone grey, so the sweeper becomes the subject at once. Tyre tracks lead the eye down the road. When an event drains colour from a scene, find the one saturated element and place it off-centre.

feed.title: Squid drying at Iwami, Tottori

image.credit: David Monniaux, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Iwami is a town in Iwami District, Tottori Prefecture, Japan. As of 1 December 2022 it had an estimated population of 10,998 and a total area of 122.32 square kilometres, and it lies entirely within the San'in Kaigan Geopark. It is San'in Kaigan's biggest international beach resort. David Monniaux photographed squid drying there in August 2003. The picture is a close vertical frame: split squid, pale and translucent, hang from ropes in a row, with their tentacles trailing, and behind them a green wooded hillside and a white boat on the water show where the catch was landed.
feed.lookAt: Hanging objects repeat down the frame like a curtain, and a shallow focus on the nearest squid separates it from the hillside and boat behind. The pale bodies against green make a calm palette. Look for a repeating food or craft element that tells you about a place.

feed.title: Hupao Spring, Hangzhou

image.credit: Sh1019, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: One of the Ten Scenes of West Lake

feed.story: Hupao, also called Dreaming of Tiger Spring, is a spring and park in southwestern Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. Its water seeps out of quartzite and has been counted among the finest in China for centuries, prized for brewing teas such as the local Longjing. Legend says wild tigers pawed the ground in the ninth century to uncover the spring for a hermit sage. It supplied the Dinghui Monastery that once stood nearby and is linked with the thirteenth-century monk Ji Gong, whose remains are enshrined close by. The spring is now one of the Ten Scenes of West Lake. Sh1019 photographed this corner on 23 June 2007.
feed.lookAt: A pale stone figure reclines beneath an overhanging rock beside a tiger shape, and the pool below repeats it upside down. The darker green wall of foliage frames the pair and lifts them out of the scene. When a subject is lighter than its surroundings, use the surroundings as the frame.

feed.title: Kuroshio Sea tank, Churaumi Aquarium

image.credit: Jordy Meow, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: 35 m long, 27 m wide, 10 m deep

feed.story: The Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium stands in the Ocean Expo Park in Okinawa, Japan. It opened on 1 November 2002, replacing the earlier Ocean Expo Aquarium. Its Kuroshio Sea tank measures 35 metres long, 27 metres wide and 10 metres deep and holds 7.5 million litres of water. The viewing window is an acrylic panel 8.2 by 22.5 metres and 60 centimetres thick, which was the largest of its kind at the time. Whale sharks swim in the tank alongside many other fish. Jordy Meow made this photograph on 26 November 2012, with visitors standing against the glass.
feed.lookAt: The visitors are pure silhouettes against the glowing blue, which gives the tank a sense of scale no measurement could. Expose for the bright water and let the crowd fall to black. Silhouettes of people beside a huge subject tell the viewer how big it is.

feed.title: Main street, Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas

image.credit: Jack Delano, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Jack Delano made this colour transparency in December 1941 and titled it View down the main street from the Grand Hotel, Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas Island, Virgin Islands. Delano was born in the Russian Empire in 1914 and worked for the Farm Security Administration, and he later spent much of his life in Puerto Rico. From a raised vantage he looks down a street that bends away between pastel buildings with a hillside of white houses behind. A Coca-Cola sign hangs on one building, two dark cars wait in the foreground, and pedestrians cross the street in late sun.
feed.lookAt: Shooting from a window or balcony lifts you above the street, so the road, the people and the hill of houses stack in layers. Long shadows show the late light on the pavement. A raised viewpoint lets you show a whole street in one frame.

caption.title: Main street, Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas

feed.title: Kasbah Taourirt, Ouarzazate

image.credit: Petar Milošević, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Kasbah Taourirt is a historic fortified residence in Ouarzazate, Morocco. Oral tradition says the Imzwarn family first built it in the seventeenth century, and the Glaoui family expanded it in the nineteenth, when it controlled a point where the Draa and Dadès valleys met along Saharan trade routes. It is built mainly of rammed earth and mud-brick, mostly three floors high, with square corner towers decorated with geometric motifs. It joined the national heritage list in 1954 and a small part was restored in the 1990s with UNESCO's help. Petar Milošević photographed it on 18 March 2024.
feed.lookAt: The pale clay walls sit as a thin band in the middle of the frame, with palms in front and a streaked sky above. The dark foreground foliage leads the eye across to the towers. Place a landmark low in the frame and let weather above it do the work.

feed.title: Iceberg in North Star Bay, Greenland

image.credit: Jeremy Harbeck, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Mouth of Wolstenholme Fjord, north-west Greenland
Pituffik Space Base, the only inhabited place on the bay

feed.story: North Star Bay, also known as Thule Harbor, lies at the mouth of Wolstenholme Fjord in north-west Greenland, with the mesa-like Mount Dundas at its north-eastern end. Knud Rasmussen founded a trading post and mission called Thule there in 1910, and the United States began building defence facilities from 1943. NASA support scientist Jeremy Harbeck took this picture in March 2015. He had arrived at Thule Air Base on 20 March, where a mechanical problem grounded the aircraft for Operation IceBridge, so he had a few days free. This picture of an iceberg under a starry sky comes from that trip.
feed.lookAt: A long exposure under a starry twilight sky turns the ice from white into soft blue, and the pink glow at the horizon tints the snow. The iceberg's angled shape points up into the sky. Shoot in the blue hour when you want both stars and detail on the ground.

caption.title: Iceberg in North Star Bay, Greenland

feed.title: Caboose, Proviso yard, Chicago

image.credit: Jack Delano, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Jack Delano titled this colour transparency Caboose on the caboose track at C & NW RR's Proviso yard, Chicago, Ill., and made it in April 1943. Delano was born in the Russian Empire in 1914 and worked for the Farm Security Administration; he later lived mostly in Puerto Rico. He photographed the yard's red Chicago and North Western cabooses in a row, each marked with the railroad's name and a number, here 12010. Parallel rails fill the bottom of the frame and a heavy grey sky fills the top. The red wooden car stands flat against the clouds like a stage set.
feed.lookAt: The caboose runs across the middle of the frame, with rails below and cloudy sky above, so the red is the only strong colour. The neighbouring cars cut off at the edges suggest a longer row. Put one saturated subject against a neutral overcast sky.

feed.title: Sea caves, Cape Greco

image.credit: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Cape Greco is a headland in south-eastern Cyprus at the southern end of Famagusta Bay, between the resorts of Ayia Napa and Protaras. It is the easternmost point of the government-controlled areas of the Republic of Cyprus. In antiquity it was known as Cape Pedalion, and Strabo wrote that the hill above it was sacred to Aphrodite. Along the coast of Cape Greco National Forest Park, sea caves called the fairy caves or Palaces are carved naturally into limestone cliffs. The area is also an Important Bird Area for migrating raptors. Kallerna took this picture on 2 October 2020 at 17:54.
feed.lookAt: Standing inside the cave, the dark arch frames a bright sky and the cliffs beyond, with low evening light turning the layered limestone gold. The rock ceiling does the framing for you. Step back into a shadowed opening and use it as a ready-made frame.

feed.title: Triumphal Arch of the Cinquantenaire, Brussels

image.credit: Marc Ryckaert, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Bronze quadriga, Brabant Raising the National Flag

feed.story: The Triumphal Arch of the Cinquantenaire in Brussels was completed in May 1905 and inaugurated by King Leopold II on 27 September that year. It commemorates fifty years of Belgian independence and was first planned for the 1880 National Exhibition, when only the column bases were finished. Gédéon Bordiau designed it and worked on it for almost twenty years. After his death in 1904 the French architect Charles Girault changed it from a single arch to a triple arch. A bronze quadriga by Jules Lagae and Thomas Vincotte, Brabant Raising the National Flag, crowns it. Marc Ryckaert photographed it on 26 June 2012.
feed.lookAt: The camera sits on the central axis of the lawn, so the three arches, the colonnades and the quadriga fall into mirror symmetry. A few small cars and walkers give scale. For monumental architecture, stand exactly on the centre line and keep the frame level.

caption.title: Triumphal Arch of the Cinquantenaire, Brussels

feed.title: 2000 block of Rhode Island Ave NE, Washington

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith photographed the 2000 block of Rhode Island Avenue NE in Washington, D.C., on 19 September 2010 at 16:20, according to the file's Exif data. The picture belongs to the George F. Landegger Collection of District of Columbia Photographs in Carol M. Highsmith's America, which she gave to the Library of Congress. Highsmith has donated her work to the Library since 1992, and the Library says all of it is in the public domain. Here she squares up to a low white-sided shop, Brown's Corner Barber Shop, under a web of power lines, with a utility pole and a traffic signal at its right.
feed.lookAt: Facing the shopfront straight on, with the camera level, keeps the horizontal siding, the wires and the pavement parallel. The pole and traffic light cut the frame vertically and the green signal is the single colour accent. Straight-on framing makes a plain street look designed.

caption.title: 2000 block of Rhode Island Ave NE, Washington
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: Charnel House, St Helen's Church, Cliffe

image.credit: Slaunger, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Cliffe is a village on the Hoo Peninsula in Kent, on a low chalk escarpment overlooking the Thames marshes. In 774, King Offa of Mercia built a wooden church there dedicated to St Helen. In a corner of its graveyard stands the charnel house, built in the mid-nineteenth century. It served as a makeshift mortuary: bodies found washed up or floating in the nearby Thames were taken there to await identification and burial. It stayed in use until the early twentieth century, when Public Health Acts ended such buildings. Slaunger photographed it on 6 May 2015.
feed.lookAt: The small building sits to the right while the flat marshland stretches away on the left, so the scene explains its job as well as its looks. Mid-morning cloud keeps the flint walls free of harsh shadow. Include the landscape around a small building to tell why it stands there.

caption.title: Charnel House, St Helen's Church, Cliffe

feed.title: Salar de Carcote

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Salar de Carcote, also called Salar de San Martín, is a salt flat in northern Chile, southwest of Ollagüe. It covers about 108 square kilometres at an elevation of 3,690 metres, and volcanoes dominate the landscape: Ollagüe to the east and Aucanquilcha to the north. The salar is what remains of an ancient lake that once connected to Lake Minchin. Small lakes now dot its shores, mostly along the west side, covering about three to four square kilometres, and the largest is Laguna Verde. Diego Delso made this panorama on 9 February 2016 at about 16:45, from the frames numbered 54 to 58.
feed.lookAt: Stitching several frames gives a wide strip in which the pale salt crust curves along the green-blue lagoon and the mountains hold the horizon. The shoreline is the leading line. When the scene is long and low, a panorama lets you keep every layer sharp.

feed.title: Arcade from Genthe's Cuba and Guatemala views

image.credit: Arnold Genthe, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Arnold Genthe made this negative, catalogued by the Library of Congress as Travel views of Cuba and Guatemala, at some point between 1899 and 1926. Genthe, born in 1869, was a German-American photographer best known for his pictures of Northern California, San Francisco's Chinatown and the 1906 earthquake, and for portraits of well-known people. This frame looks down a shaded arcade of heavy round columns toward an arch. Beyond it a battered plaster wall carries a barred window and a closed wooden door, and a strip of bright paving crosses the foreground. The Library's record names no further date or location for this particular view.
feed.lookAt: The columns at right step away in a row and the arch frames the far wall, so the eye is pulled from the foreground into the light at the back. Hard sun makes bands of shade across the floor. In an arcade, line up the arch and use the columns as repeating shapes.

caption.title: Arcade from Genthe's Cuba and Guatemala views

feed.title: Fog in the Synevyr valleys

image.credit: Rbrechko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Synevyr National Nature Park lies in Zakarpattia Oblast, in south-western Ukraine, in the Carpathians. It was established in 1974 and covers 40,400 hectares, with headquarters in Khust. Its main attractions include Lake Synevyr, which became a Ramsar wetland in 2004, and a brown bear sanctuary. Since 13 July 2017 four of its sections, Darvaika, Kvasovets, Strymba and Vilshany, have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing of Carpathian and other European beech primeval forests. The photographer Rbrechko made this photograph on 20 October 2017 at about nine in the morning.
feed.lookAt: Morning fog fills the valley like water, and the red and gold autumn trees in the foreground stand clear above it. The hill ridges fade into progressively paler blue. Climb above the mist, shoot in early light, and let each layer fade lighter into the distance.

feed.title: Mount Shasta over Lake Siskiyou

image.credit: Radomianin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Lake Siskiyou is a reservoir formed by Box Canyon Dam on the Sacramento River in far northern California, near the town of Mount Shasta. It is used for recreation, watershed protection and flood control. Above it rises Mount Shasta, a stratovolcano at the southern end of the Cascade Range, 4,322 metres high, the second-highest peak in the Cascades. It has seven named glaciers, the largest of which are Whitney, Bolam, Hotlum and Wintun. The Karuk call it Úytaahkoo. Radomianin photographed it from the southwest on 16 March 2024, with the Wagon Creek footbridge at the left.
feed.lookAt: The snowy cone sits above a band of dark conifers and a wide strip of blue water that covers the lower third. The small footbridge at left gives a scale. Divide the frame into three flat bands and let one clean peak be the point.

feed.title: Elliðaey, Westman Islands

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Elliðaey is a small, uninhabited island south of Iceland, the north-easternmost of the Westman Islands, which number 15 to 18 islands and smaller rocks. It covers 0.45 square kilometres and is believed to have formed in an eruption five to six thousand years ago. A hunting lodge built in 1953 stands on it. The island is privately owned and run by the Elliðaey Hunting Association, and it is reached by boat from the mainland and by a rope on its lower east side. Diego Delso photographed the island from the sea on 17 August 2014 in the afternoon.
feed.lookAt: Shot from the water, the green-capped cliffs lie as a single dark band between an empty sea and a pale sky. The small white lodge at the left shows the island's size. Keep the horizon low and still, and let a tiny man-made detail show the scale.

feed.title: Glacier Point at sunset, Yosemite

image.credit: Diliff, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Yosemite Valley, Half Dome, Yosemite Falls

feed.story: Glacier Point is a viewpoint above Yosemite Valley in California, on the south wall of the valley at 7,214 feet, or 2,199 metres, about 3,200 feet above Curry Village. It looks across to Yosemite Valley, Yosemite Falls, Half Dome, Vernal Fall, Nevada Fall and Clouds Rest. Between 1872 and 1968 it was the site of the Yosemite Firefall. This wide panorama by the photographer Diliff, made on 16 May 2013 around sunset, looks from roughly north on the left to east on the right, across the valley and the granite dome beyond.
feed.lookAt: Soft pink light colours the cloud and warms the top of the granite dome while the valley below falls into shadow. The wide panorama lets the dome and a thin waterfall at right share one image. At sunset, let the shadows go dark and expose for the lit rock.

feed.title: Mosque at Douar Chiker, Taza

image.credit: Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: This is the south facade of the Sheker, or Shakir, Mosque in Douar Chiker, in Taza Province, Morocco. The village lies in Daya Chiker, a polje depression in the Fez-Meknes region in the north-east of the country. The climate there is Mediterranean, and agriculture has been practised in the area since the late Neolithic period. Tourism is growing because of the adjacent Tazekka National Park. Timothy A. Gonsalves photographed the mosque on 4 November 2025 at 17:34, in the last hour of daylight, with a tall pink-trimmed minaret rising over a cream building and a wooded hillside behind it.
feed.lookAt: The tall minaret splits the frame vertically and its pink edging stands out against a clean blue sky, while the thin cloud at left adds some movement. A slightly low viewpoint keeps the tower upright. For a tall, simple building, choose a clear sky and keep the verticals straight.

feed.title: Baspa Valley after snowfall, Sangla

image.credit: UnpetitproleX, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Baspa, Sangla on its right bank

feed.story: Sangla is a town in the Baspa Valley of the Kinnaur district in Himachal Pradesh, India, close to the border with Tibet. It sits at 2,650 metres on the right bank of the Baspa River and is the administrative headquarters of Sangla tehsil. Winter temperatures there can fall to minus 15 degrees Celsius, and the page on the town describes about 270 millimetres of snowfall. UnpetitproleX photographed the valley after a snowfall on 17 March 2025 at 08:22. A yellow building stands at the left, frost coats the bare trees in the middle ground, and snow-covered ridges climb to the sunlit peaks.
feed.lookAt: Morning sun from the upper left leaves the foreground snow lit and the valley wall in blue shadow. The frosted tree stands as a bright shape against the dark slope. After fresh snow, shoot early, when low light still gives the white surface a visible texture.

feed.title: Steel bridge near San Mateo, Peru

image.credit: David Gubler (Kabelleger), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Callao and Lima to La Oroya

feed.story: Two General Electric C30-7 locomotives, numbers 1008 and 1009 of the Ferrocarril Central Andino, cross a steel bridge between Rio Blanco and San Mateo in Peru. San Mateo is a district of Huarochirí Province in the Department of Lima. The railway runs 535 kilometres from the port of Callao through Lima and along the Rímac River, crossing the Galera Tunnel at 4,783 metres on its way to La Oroya. Construction began in January 1870, and the original line needed about 58 bridges and 69 tunnels. David Gubler photographed this crossing on 14 July 2013 for his railway picture site.
feed.lookAt: The red-and-yellow locomotives sit exactly on the diagonal of the bridge, with the cliff leaning in from the right and the yellow girders echoing the train. The bright blue sky isolates them. Time the shutter for the moment the train is fully on the span, with the whole bridge in frame.

caption.title: Steel bridge near San Mateo, Peru

feed.title: Kansai at night from Mount Rokko

image.credit: Laitr Keiows, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Mount Rokko rises above Kobe in Hyōgo, Japan, and the Rokko Cable Line, a funicular that opened in 1932, climbs its slope between two stations 493 metres apart in height. The line is 1.7 kilometres long, and Kobe Rokko Railway operates it. From the Tenrandai platform on the mountain, the lights of the Kansai urban area spread out below. Laitr Keiows made this panorama on 6 January 2012, a winter night. A dark pine branch hangs at the left, and a bright band of the city runs along the shore to the far right under a black sky.
feed.lookAt: A very wide, shallow panorama turns the city into a glittering strip between black sky and black hills. The branch at the left gives a dark frame and some depth. At night, use a tripod, a low ISO and a wide format, and let the empty dark areas be part of the composition.

caption.title: Kansai at night from Mount Rokko

feed.title: Wildlife feeding station, S-charl

image.credit: Agnes Monkelbaan, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: S-charl is a village in the municipality of Scuol, in the canton of Graubünden, Switzerland. It lies in the Engadin region at 1,810 metres in the Val S-charl, south of Scuol, in the Sesvenna Range of the Swiss Alps. The Clemgia, a tributary of the Inn, runs past it with rapids near the village. Agnes Monkelbaan photographed a wildlife feeding station there on 12 October 2024 at about midday. The small wooden shed has slatted sides and a painted white wall showing deer, and it stands on a green slope among larch trees whose needles have turned yellow in autumn.
feed.lookAt: Yellow larch needles at the upper left and the dark trunks give a calm autumn frame around the shed. The white wall with painted deer is the brightest area, so the eye goes there first. In woodland, look for the one pale surface and build the frame around it.

feed.title: Condor geoglyph, Nazca Lines

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Nazca lines are geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru. People created them between 500 BC and 500 AD by removing the top layer of reddish-brown, iron-oxide-coated pebbles to reveal a yellow-grey subsoil. The lines are typically 10 to 15 centimetres deep, and the combined length of all of them is more than 1,300 kilometres. Some of the shapes are best seen from the air, at around 500 metres, and the largest are about 370 metres long. This frame, taken on 29 July 2015, is an aerial view of the figure known as the Condor. The site became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994.
feed.lookAt: Seen from above, the Condor is only a few thin pale lines on tan ground, and straight lines cross it at sharp angles. Notice how the pale line against dark soil keeps its shape even though the colours are quiet. When you shoot from a window or drone, look for line and contrast first.

feed.title: Orchards in snow, Sangla

image.credit: UnpetitproleX, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Close to the border with Tibet

feed.story: Sangla is a town in the Baspa Valley, in the Kinnaur District of Himachal Pradesh in northern India, close to the border with Tibet. It is the administrative headquarters of the Sangla tehsil and the main town of the valley, which is also called the Sangla Valley. This picture shows apple and walnut orchards after a night of snowfall. According to the photographer, this is where the Kinnauri apples come from, and the snow is essential for their growth. The photograph was taken on 17 March 2025 at 8:31 in the morning, when the fresh snow still clung to the branches.
feed.lookAt: Fresh snow on every branch turns the orchard into one pale texture, and the dark forested ridge behind it gives that texture an edge to rest against. Shoot snow soon after it falls, in clear morning light, and put something dark behind it so the white reads as white.

feed.title: Jefferson Memorial at dusk

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith made this photograph of the Jefferson Memorial in Washington, D.C., at dusk, on a colour transparency. The Library of Congress catalogues it as made between 1980 and 2006 and notes no known restrictions on publication. Highsmith, born in 1946, began her nationwide photography project after extensively photographing the Willard Hotel in the early 1980s for its restoration. She has donated her photographs to the Library of Congress since 1992, creating a collection of nearly 100,000 images, all in the public domain. Her work documents the landscapes, architecture and people of the United States.
feed.lookAt: The marble glows from within against a deep violet sky, and the still water below repeats the blue. Shoot in the minutes after sunset, when the sky and floodlights balance. Keep the building centred and low, with the dark trees on each side to frame it.

caption.title: Jefferson Memorial at dusk
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: Mount Bradley, Alaska

image.credit: Ross Fowler, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Mount Bradley stands in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough in Alaska. The borough, often called the Mat-Su Borough, has Palmer as its seat, and Wasilla is its largest incorporated community. It contains the entire Matanuska and Susitna Rivers, which empty into Cook Inlet on the borough's southern border, and it is one of the few agricultural areas in Alaska. The 2020 census counted 107,081 people living there. Ross Fowler photographed the peak on 3 June 2014 at 11:28 in the morning with a few clouds drifting past its snow-streaked summit on a bright, mostly blue early-summer day.
feed.lookAt: The summit sits near the top centre and the rock face fills the frame below it, so the eye climbs the ridge line to the cloud. Fill the frame with the subject when the shape of the mountain is the story, and let one small cloud mark the peak.

feed.title: Flower Dome and Cloud Forest, Gardens by the Bay

image.credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Gardens by the Bay is an urban park of 105 hectares in the Central Region of Singapore, next to the Marina Reservoir. It has three waterfront gardens. The largest is Bay South Garden, 54 hectares, designed by Grant Associates, and its Flower Dome is the largest glass greenhouse in the world. Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong first announced the project at the National Day Rally in 2005, as part of the plan to turn the Garden City into a City in a Garden. The park had 6.4 million visitors in 2014. Uwe Aranas took this picture on 20 February 2015, looking down at the two domes from above.
feed.lookAt: From above, the two glass shells become curved shapes against flat green water, and the paths curve with them. A high viewpoint turns a building into a graphic design. Look for the repeated curve and keep the horizon out so the shape does the work.

caption.title: Flower Dome and Cloud Forest, Gardens by the Bay

feed.title: Scotty's Castle, Death Valley

image.credit: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Carol M. Highsmith photographed Scotty's Castle in Death Valley, California, on 19 December 2012. Her notes describe it as an anomalous attraction, removed from most of the park in its far-northern reaches near the Nevada border. The elegant home, properly called Death Valley Ranch, is a window into the life and times of the Roaring 1920s and Depression 1930s. Chicago millionaire Albert Mussey Johnson built it in the early 1920s as a vacation getaway. Highsmith has donated her photographs to the Library of Congress since 1992, and all of them are in the public domain.
feed.lookAt: A clear winter sky is a flat dark blue above the whitewashed walls and red tile roofs, and the tower stands off-centre. Choose a straight-on, level view for architecture so the lines stay upright. Winter sun keeps the walls evenly lit and the colours clean.

caption.title: Scotty's Castle, Death Valley
caption.line2: Carol M. Highsmith · Library of Congress

feed.title: West Maroon Creek, Maroon Bells area

image.credit: Rhododendrites, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Maroon Bells are two peaks in the Elk Mountains of Colorado, about 19 kilometres southwest of Aspen. Maroon Peak rises to 4,317 metres and North Maroon Peak to 4,273 metres, and both are fourteeners. The view of them from the Maroon Creek valley is very heavily photographed, and the surrounding Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness was one of five areas in Colorado designated as wilderness in the original Wilderness Act of 1964. Rhododendrites made this picture on 1 August 2017, at 1:34 in the afternoon, of a body of water along West Maroon Creek, southwest of Maroon Lake, facing east-northeast.
feed.lookAt: Midday puffy clouds duplicate themselves in the still water, and the hillside is mirrored almost evenly. When the light is too harsh for a grand view, turn to the reflection. Wait for the water to go still, and keep the horizon near the middle so both halves carry the scene.

caption.title: West Maroon Creek, Maroon Bells area

feed.title: View from Mt Fyffe, Kaikōura Ranges

image.credit: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Kaikōura Ranges are two parallel ranges of mountains in the Canterbury Region, in the northeast of New Zealand's South Island. They are visible from a great distance, including from the southern coast of the North Island. Michal Klajban took this panorama from Mount Fyffe on 20 October 2019 at 2:03 in the afternoon. It looks across a bare, rounded ridge toward the snow-patched main crest, with ridges stacked behind each other until they fade into haze. It is a wide frame, more than twice as wide as it is tall.
feed.lookAt: A wide crop lets the ridge in the foreground lead into the snowy crest, and each ridge behind it is a little paler. Use the tonal steps to show distance. Put something close and textured at the bottom of the frame, then let the layers stack above it.

caption.title: View from Mt Fyffe, Kaikōura Ranges

feed.title: Side shows at the Vermont state fair

image.credit: Jack Delano, Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Jack Delano photographed the side shows at the Vermont state fair in Rutland in September 1941, on colour slide film. Delano was born Yakov Ovcharov in the Russian Empire in 1914. In the United States he worked for the Works Progress Administration and most notably for the Farm Security Administration, and he was also a composer, a filmmaker and a poet who spent much of his life in Puerto Rico. This frame looks down on the fairground from above. A Ferris wheel and striped tents surround a round carousel tent, and visitors walk across the dusty ground.
feed.lookAt: Shot from above, the Ferris wheel, round tent and striped awnings sort into separate shapes, and the small figures below keep it human. Find a high spot over a busy scene, then wait for people to spread out across open ground so the shapes stay clear.

caption.title: Side shows at the Vermont state fair

feed.title: Half Dome from Glacier Point

image.credit: Diliff, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Yosemite National Park in California covers 1,187 square miles, in four counties, and has been a World Heritage Site since 1984. It is known for its granite cliffs, waterfalls, clear streams, giant sequoia groves, lakes, meadows, glaciers and biological diversity, and almost 95 percent of it is designated wilderness. About ten million years ago, the Sierra Nevada was uplifted and tilted, which steepened stream beds and cut deep, narrow canyons. About a million years ago, glaciers formed at higher elevations. Diliff photographed Half Dome from Glacier Point on 16 May 2013, with soft clouds streaking the sky behind the granite.
feed.lookAt: Warm low light picks out the sheer face of Half Dome while the ridges beside it stay in cool shade. That split between warm and cool separates the subject from its surroundings. Arrive early or stay late, and expose for the lit rock.

feed.title: Shingo La, Zanskar

image.credit: Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Zanskar Range spans Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh in northern India and separates the Zanskar valley from the Indus valley. It lies between the Great Himalayas and the Ladakh Range, and some of its peaks are higher than 6,500 metres. Timothy A. Gonsalves photographed this view on 4 October 2022 from Shingo La, at 5,054 metres, looking north toward the Lungnak valley. The Darcha-Padum road, which was under construction, descends from the pass toward Lungnak and on to Padum. According to the photographer, there is much less snow on this north side of the pass than on the south, Lahaul side.
feed.lookAt: The unfinished road curls into the lower left and shows how big the valley is, because the machines on it look tiny. Include one small human-made thing to give scale to a mountain scene, and let the snow line show which slope faces the sun.

feed.title: Mount Bromo at sunrise

image.credit: Thomas Hirsch, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Bromo is an active somma volcano in the Tengger mountains of East Java, Indonesia. At 2,329 metres it is not the highest peak of the massif, but it is the most active and famous, and a Hindu pilgrimage site. The name comes from the Javanese pronunciation of Brahma, the Hindu god of creation. Bromo sits in a plain called the Sea of Sand, a nature reserve protected since 1919. Thomas Hirsch took this picture at sunrise on 26 September 2002, showing Bromo's smoking crater, Semeru smoking in the background, and Batok in the foreground, with early morning fog covering the plain of fine volcanic ash.
feed.lookAt: Fog fills the plain like water and leaves the volcanoes standing as separate islands, and the plume above Semeru marks the farthest peak. Get high before sunrise, then use the haze to separate each layer, with the darkest cone in front and the palest peak at the back.

feed.title: Spiti River valley above Kaza

image.credit: Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Spiti is a high-altitude region of the Himalayas in north-eastern Himachal Pradesh. Its name means the middle land, between Tibet and India, and it includes the valley of the Spiti River. It has a cold desert environment and is among the least populated regions of India. Timothy A. Gonsalves photographed this scene on 23 June 2018 from the left bank of the river, about 15 kilometres above Kaza. The road NH505 runs along the opposite bank in a narrow valley. The river has cut a gorge about 100 metres deep, and the river bed is at 3,820 metres.
feed.lookAt: Pale gullies run down the slope like the veins of a leaf, and the braided river across the bottom repeats the pattern. Shooting across the valley from the far bank flattens it into stripes. Look for a repeating shape and crop tight so nothing else competes.

feed.title: Fields below Yugar, Tsarap River

image.credit: Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Eastern part of the Zanskar valley

feed.story: The Tsarap River, also known as Tsarap Chu, forms the eastern part of the Zanskar valley in Ladakh, India. The river is 182 kilometres long, and villages along its banks use it to irrigate their fields. It is also used by tourists for adventure sports. Timothy A. Gonsalves photographed this scene on 4 June 2024 at 3:24 in the afternoon. It shows fields below Yugar, which lies at 3,850 metres, on the left bank of the Tsarap, opposite Phuktal. The turquoise river bends through bare brown mountains, and the green of the irrigated fields follows its course.
feed.lookAt: Colour does the work here: a ribbon of turquoise water and a strip of green fields cut through brown rock. When the land is mostly one colour, find the one contrasting colour and use it to lead the eye in. Place it on a diagonal.

feed.title: Strokkur erupting, Haukadalur

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Strokkur is a fountain-type geyser in the Haukadalur geothermal area, beside the Hvítá River in southwest Iceland, east of Reykjavík. Its Icelandic name means churn. It typically erupts every six to ten minutes, usually to a height of 15 to 20 metres, though it can sometimes reach 40 metres. Diego Delso photographed it on 16 August 2014 at 1:21 in the afternoon, at the instant before the eruption, when the water swells into a pale blue dome. A line of visitors stands waiting in the distance, under a deep blue sky and a large cloud.
feed.lookAt: The blue dome of water bulges just before the burst, and the small row of people shows how big it is. Because Strokkur repeats every few minutes, you can wait and try again. Learn the rhythm, frame the vertical space above it, and press at the swelling.

feed.title: Pheriche at sunset

image.credit: Babin Dulal, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Pheriche is a village in the Khumbu region of eastern Nepal, about 4,371 metres above sea level and above the Tsola River. It is a popular stop for trekkers and climbers and an important acclimatization stopover on the way to Everest Base Camp, with over 25 local guest houses. The village was originally a farming settlement that raised potatoes and buckwheat and kept yaks. A hospital managed by the Himalayan Rescue Association opens only in the two trekking seasons. Babin Dulal photographed the village at sunset on 18 March 2019, when the last light turned a high summit gold above the lodges.
feed.lookAt: The sun has already left the village, but a high peak still glows gold and smoke from the lodges softens the middle ground. Wait for the last light on the summit, and keep the dim foreground in the frame. The contrast with the dark valley is what makes the glow.

feed.title: Glacial lake below Cho La, Chola Valley

image.credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Cho La is a summit pass 5,420 metres above sea level in the Solukhumbu District of northeastern Nepal. It connects the village of Dzongla to the east with the village of Thagnak to the west. Vyacheslav Argenberg took this picture on 18 October 2009 at 11:49 in the morning while descending from the pass into the Chola Valley, at about 5,200 metres. It looks east across a glacial lake and snow-covered rocks toward Ama Dablam, 6,810 metres high, and other Himalayan peaks of Mahalangur Himal. Three trekkers walk across the snow in the foreground.
feed.lookAt: The trekkers sit in the lower left and the lake leads across to Ama Dablam, so the walkers give the eye a path and a measure of size. Place people along the lines of the scene and let them look small against the peaks.

caption.title: Glacial lake below Cho La, Chola Valley

feed.title: Chuquicamata open-pit mine

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Chuquicamata is a state-owned copper mine just outside Calama in northern Chile, at 2,850 metres above sea level. By excavated volume it is the largest open-pit copper mine in the world. The pit is 3.5 kilometres long and 4.5 kilometres wide, and at 850 metres deep it is the second deepest open-pit mine, after Bingham Canyon in Utah. Work began in 1882 to extract gold and copper, and it is now owned by the Chilean company Codelco. In April 2019 Chuquicamata started to extract minerals from a new underground mine. Diego Delso photographed the interior on 1 February 2016.
feed.lookAt: Terraced benches fill the frame from edge to edge and small trucks sit on them, so the pit's size is visible at once. A tall vertical crop with no sky turns an industrial scene into a pattern. Look for repeated lines and a few small things to give scale.

feed.title: Old lighthouse, Akranes

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Akranes, about 50 km north of Reykjavík

feed.story: The old lighthouse of Akranes stands at the westernmost point of the Akranes Peninsula in Iceland. It is one of the oldest concrete lighthouses in the country. Built in 1918, it served the fishing town of Akranes until it was deactivated in 1947 in favour of a larger structure several metres away. Akranes itself is a port town on the west coast of Iceland, about 50 kilometres north of Reykjavík, in an area that was settled in the 9th century. Diego Delso photographed the lighthouse on 14 August 2014 at 9:39 in the morning, with dark waves lapping at the orange-lichened rocks in the foreground.
feed.lookAt: The white tower sits small against the wide sea, and the rocky shoreline carries the eye to it from the lower right. Leave empty space around a small subject so it stands out. Use a line, like this shore, to lead into the frame.

feed.title: Rapanui Rock at sunset, Sumner

image.credit: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Rapanui Rock (Shag Rock), a sea stack
Shattered in the February 2011 Christchurch earthquake

feed.story: Shag Rock, also known as Rapanui, is a sea stack at the entrance of the Avon Heathcote Estuary near Christchurch, New Zealand. It is a prominent landmark for navigators at sea and for travellers on the road to Sumner. The rock stands close to the southern shore, just above the low-tide level. In the February 2011 Christchurch earthquake it shattered, and its remains, still easily seen from the road, have been called Shag Pile by some locals. Michal Klajban photographed it on 20 July 2020 at 4:41 in the afternoon, with low sun glowing under layered clouds.
feed.lookAt: The broken stack is a dark silhouette against a band of glowing sky, and the wet sand returns the glow. Shoot toward low sun and expose for the bright sky so the rock goes dark. Put the horizon low so the layered clouds fill the frame.

feed.title: Valley of Flowers National Park

image.credit: Rohit Sharma, UnpetitproleX, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Valley of Flowers National Park, established 1982
87.50 km², about 8 km long and 2 km wide

feed.story: Valley of Flowers National Park, in Chamoli in Uttarakhand, India, was established in 1982 and is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers. It lies at 3,352 to 3,658 metres above sea level, covers 87.5 square kilometres, and is about eight kilometres long and two wide. Together with Nanda Devi National Park to the east it forms a transition zone between the Zanskar and Great Himalayan ranges. Rare animals live there, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard and musk deer. The photograph is dated 16 August 2022, at 12:50 in the afternoon, and shows pink and white flowers in the foreground.
feed.lookAt: Pink and white flowers fill the foreground and the valley narrows behind them toward a distant gap in the cloud. Get low among the blooms so they become the foreground, then let the V-shaped valley lead toward the far end.

feed.title: Lac Gentau and Pic du Midi d'Ossau

image.credit: Myrabella, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: Lac Gentau is a lake in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, in the French Pyrenees. At an elevation of 1,947.3 metres, its surface area is 0.093 square kilometres. Myrabella photographed it on 28 July 2010 as it reflects the Pic du Midi d'Ossau, the rocky peak rising behind the water. The picture shows a green, grassy shore dotted with grazing sheep, and a thin stream winding in from the lower left. A walker is visible near the shore, and a single cloud sits above the mountain, which is mirrored in the still, deep blue water.
feed.lookAt: The stream curves in from the lower left, the lake spreads in the middle, and the peak and its reflection finish the line. Use a winding foreground element to carry the viewer toward the mountain, and let the reflection double its weight.

caption.title: Lac Gentau and Pic du Midi d'Ossau

feed.title: Salt ponds of Maras

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

facts: Salt Mines of Maras, Urubamba Province

feed.story: The Salt Mines of Maras are one of the largest salt extraction centres of pre-Hispanic origin in Cusco, in southeast Peru, at 3,200 metres above sea level. Salt has been harvested there since the time of the Inca Empire. The site has around 3,000 ponds of about five square metres each. Because the surrounding mountains are salty, underground water deposits brine in the ponds, and the water evaporates in the sun. After about a month the salt reaches ten centimetres deep and is removed in sacks. Diego Delso photographed the ponds on 30 July 2015.
feed.lookAt: The white terraces step down the slope as a mosaic of small rectangles, each divided by low brown walls. Shoot from above at an angle so the walls draw a grid. A pale surface under blue sky is bright, so watch your exposure to keep the salt from clipping.

feed.title: The Hummingbird geoglyph, Nazca

image.credit: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

feed.story: The Nazca lines are a group of geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru. People created them between 500 BC and 500 AD by removing the reddish-brown, iron-oxide-coated pebbles of the desert floor to reveal a yellow-grey subsoil. The lines are typically 10 to 15 centimetres deep, and their combined length is more than 1,300 kilometres. Most run straight across the landscape, but some form animals and plants, and the Hummingbird is one of the most popular. The geoglyphs are spread over an 80 kilometre plateau between the towns of Nazca and Palpa. Diego Delso photographed the Hummingbird from the air on 29 July 2015.
